title: Each reduced cylindrical block has a positive invariant interacting Friedrichs Hamiltonian

hamiltonian.form: h_N[Psi]=1/2||grad Psi||^2+integral V_N|Psi|^2 on a finite reduced coordinate block
hamiltonian.closure: The nonnegative coercive polynomial potential gives a densely defined closed semibounded quadratic form
hamiltonian.operator: The Friedrichs operator H_N is self-adjoint, bounded below and has compact resolvent because V_N tends to infinity in finite dimension
hamiltonian.gauge_compatibility: V_N is residual-circle invariant, so H_N strongly commutes with the Haar projector and restricts self-adjointly to H_N^U(1)
hamiltonian.continuum_boundary: Quartic mode projection changes effective lower-block interactions; no compatible infinite-dimensional Gaussian family, renormalized Hamiltonian or cutoff-stable BRST complex is supplied
hamiltonian.pde_boundary: K1413's lifted-current and radial-coefficient leakage terms are unchanged, so finite-block spectral positivity does not prove global nonlinear PDE evolution
